**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 24 sits at (indeed fully satisfies) the preferred position on every material term:

- **§ 24.1** — we may assign to an Affiliate or to an M&A/asset-sale successor without Vendor consent; only prompt written notice and assignee assumption required.
- **§ 24.2** — Vendor cannot assign, delegate material performance, or transfer by change of control without our prior written consent (reasonableness-qualified for a capable, financially sound assignee), and never to a direct competitor.
- **§ 24.3** — residual assignments use a mutual "not unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed" standard.
- **§ 24.4** — our change of control gives Vendor no right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service, plus a cooperation obligation for successor administration.
- **§ 13.3** — licence rights travel with a permitted assignment, closing the usual gap.

I checked for hidden Vendor exit rights: a full-document search on "change of control" and "assign" surfaced nothing adverse. The only other relevant provision, § 9.2, is an ordinary mutual insolvency termination right that expressly carves out lawful reorganizations that do not impair performance — not a change-of-control trigger against us.
